 CORAM:
HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE VIKAS MAHAJAN  OR % 14.09.2023 CRL.M.A. 24848/2023(exemption)
1. Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
2. Application stands disposed of.

3. The present petition has been filed seeking quashing of the FIR No.221/2019 under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC registered at Police Station Bindapur, Delhi on the ground that the parties have entered into a settlement.
4. Issue notice.
Learned APP for the State accepts notice.

He submits that since the present FIR arises out of a matrimonial dispute and the parties have entered into a settlement, the State has no objection, in case the FIR is This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 21/09/2023 at 20:35:36 quashed.

5. The petitioner no.1 (former husband) and the petitioners no.2 to 5, who are close relatives of petitioner No.1, as well as, the respondent no.2 (former wife) are present in Court and they have been identified by their respective counsels and by the Investigating Officer IO, SI Anup Rana, PS.
Bindapur.
6.
The brief facts of the case are that the marriage between the parties was solemnised on 29.10.2015 as per the Hindu Rites and Customs at Delhi.
No child was born out from the said wedlock.

sentences.text: Due to temperamental differences, certain disputes arose between the parties and they started living separately w.e.f. 22.02.2018.
The dispute between the parties also led to the registration of the aforesaid FIR.

8. During the pendency of the proceedings the parties were referred to the Counselling Cell of Family Courts, Dwarka, New Delhi, where the parties arrived at a settlement, terms whereof were reduced in writing in the form of report dated 26.09.2022.
9.

entities.text: Counselling Cell of Family Courts, Dwarka
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: In terms of the said settlement, the parties agreed to dissolve their marriage by mutual consent in accordance with law.

Accordingly, the parties have obtained a decree of divorce dated 24.05.2023,
which is annexed as Annexure P-3 to the present petition.

10. It is also a term of the settlement that the petitioner no.1 shall pay a total sum of Rs.5,50,000/-
to the respondent no.2 towards full and final settlement of all her claims on account of maintenance (past, present and future), permanent alimony, stree dhan and dowry articles.
Out of the said amount, a sum of Rs.4,00,000/- has already been paid by the petitioner no.1 to the respondent no.2 in the manner as mentioned in MoU/Settlement, the
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 21/09/2023 at 20:35:36 receipt of which respondent no.2 acknowledges.

The remaining amount of Rs.1,50,000/- has been paid by the petitioner no.1 to the respondent no.2 today in the court by way of Demand Draft bearing no.506695 dated 21.07.2023 issued by the ICICI Bank, Connaught Place, New Delhi in favour of respondent no.2/Vanshika Singh.
11. The respondent no.2 who is present in Court acknowledges having receipt the entire settlement amount of Rs. 5,50,000/-.
12. On a query made by this court, the respondent no.2 states that she has no objection in case the FIR is quashed.
13. In view of the fact that the parties have arrived at a settlement, no useful purpose will be served in continuing the proceedings, rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
14. It is, thus, in the interest of justice that the present FIR and all the other proceedings emanating therefrom be quashed.

15. Consequently, the petition is allowed and the FIR No. 221/2019 under Sections 498A/506/34 IPC registered at Police Station Bindapur, Delhi alongwith all other proceedings emanating therefrom, is quashed.
16. The petition stands disposed of in the above terms.
17. Order be uploaded on the website of this court.
